description: We are an enthusiastic team of young engineers who are studying at the National Technical University of Ukraine “Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute”. Our mission is to popularise science and make it not only accessible, but interesting for everyone. We are sure that the future is in the hands of the youth; therefore, we’re here to prove it!
summary:
We've created an interactive educational tool, "Celestial Guide," about NASA's Discarded Equipment, its history, and purpose. 
Our project not only quotes scientific terms, but it also reveals the fascinating journey of each spaceship in it. We've personified each spacecraft, which only made the missions more thrilling.
Why is it important? Scientific articles usually cannot hold one's attention for too long and are even more often considered boring. Our project is meant to make education interesting and engaging, so young students and newcomers to science can learn new information through game-like interaction.
details: Built for both young space enthusiasts and complete newcomers, our interactive web experience immerses users in aerospace engineering through first-person storytelling—giving a direct voice to the spacecraft humanity has left across the solar system. Grounded in research on how strongly young audiences learn through empathy, our script balances emotional resonance with rigorous science. our interface serves two audiences at once: newcomers get pulled in by the emotional, first-person voice of the spacecraft, while curious tech enthusiasts can inspect real engineering details. Stories are powered by verified mission data from NASA and international space agencies, delivered via a fast, lightweight, and universally accessible HTML/CSS web platform so it loads instantly on low-end laptops and PCs, older school computers, and slow internet connections—removing technical barriers so any student or teacher can use it immediately without installing apps.
